title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a typed letter, dated 4.1.67 (most likely 4 January 1967), from Grothendieck to John Coates. It gives instructions for the written version of Grothendieck's talk on algebraic cycles. Its content corresponds closely to the text published as 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay Colloquium 1968, OUP 1969).

The lettering is shifted relative to the published paper, and the next page confirms this. Here:
- The index conjecture is the Hodge standard conjecture: the Hodge-Riemann sign condition on primitive algebraic classes.
- A_l(X,xi) is the Lefschetz-type condition: L_xi^{n-2i} maps the algebraic classes C^i_l bijectively onto C^{n-i}_l.
- B_l(X) is plausibly 'homological = numerical equivalence', the published conjecture D. This fits 'A + index implies B' (Bombay: A + Hodge implies D) and 'A_l(X,xi) = B_l(X) once the index theorem holds'.
- C_l(X,xi) is a polarization-dependent condition, plausibly the algebraicity of the operator Lambda, the published B. It is stable under products, specialization and hyperplane sections. It is equivalent to A(XxX) + A(YxY) + ... along a chain of hyperplane sections, as in the Corollary (v) on the next page.
- D is unspecified on this page; perhaps the Kunneth condition.
- The letter C is used twice. 'C(X) is of finite dimension over Q' refers to the Q-space of algebraic cycle classes modulo homological equivalence, not to the condition C.

The page's points, in order:
1. Expository strategy. State the index conjecture right after the Hodge theory results, and say that it gains its full meaning only together with A.
2. Characteristic 0 facts.
   - The index theorem holds (classical Hodge theory).
   - A_l to D_l are independent of l, by comparison with Betti cohomology. They are then equivalent to the statements over Q.
   - A is independent of the polarization because it is equivalent to B (hom = num). B implies A: duality of C^i and C^{n-i} plus hard Lefschetz injectivity give equal dimensions, hence bijectivity. A plus Hodge index gives B.
   - C is independent of the polarization because it can be written as A(XxX) + A(YxY) + ...
   - Since C(X) is finite-dimensional over Q, A amounts to dim C^i = dim C^{n-i}. This is visibly independent of xi; the blank in the typescript is presumably xi.
3. Characteristic p. Finite-dimensionality over Q of the algebraic cycle classes is not known. Grothendieck retracts a claim from his talk: it is not clear to him that A_l(X,xi) and C_l(X,xi) are independent of xi. Coates should either prove this or flag the possible dependence, and also flag that independence of l is not known a priori.
4. (Next page) If the index theorem holds for X, then A_l(X,xi) = B_l(X) is independent of xi.

All of this is correct and was in fact the state of knowledge.
errors: No mathematical errors. The letter C is overloaded: once as the condition C(X), once as the space of algebraic cycle classes C(X), C^i. The displayed formula C(X) = (A(XxX)+A(YxY)+..) is shorthand for the conjunction of conditions, not an equation.
There is a blank in 'independant of    )'; the intended symbol (xi, the polarization) was never typed in.
Typos: 'bu that' should be 'but that'; 'one's' should be 'ones'; 'independant/dependance' is Grothendieck's habitual spelling.

ideas.what: Place the Hodge index (standard) conjecture right after Hodge theory, and note that A + index implies hom = num.
ideas.modern_name: Hodge standard conjecture; Lefschetz standard conjecture + Hodge standard conjecture implies conjecture D

ideas.what: In characteristic 0 the conditions are independent of l via Betti comparison; A is equivalent to hom = num; A amounts to dim C^i = dim C^{n-i}, hence is independent of the polarization.
ideas.modern_name: l-independence and polarization-independence of the standard conjectures in characteristic 0

ideas.what: The polarization-dependent condition C (plausibly algebraicity of Lambda) is expressed as A(XxX) + A(YxY) + ... along hyperplane sections.
ideas.modern_name: B(X) iff Lefschetz standard conjecture for XxX (and reduction to critical degrees)
ideas.where_published: The B(X) <=> A(XxX) form is in the Bombay paper and Kleiman 1968; the hyperplane-chain form is unsure

ideas.what: Warning that in characteristic p neither independence of A_l(X,xi), C_l(X,xi) from xi nor independence from l is known, and that finite-dimensionality over Q of cycle classes is unknown.
ideas.modern_name: Open dependence of the standard conjectures on l and on the polarization in positive characteristic
ideas.where_published: Kleiman, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (1968); 'The standard conjectures' (1994)

missed.claim: Archival evidence that Coates drafted the write-up of Grothendieck's talk on algebraic cycles (the text behind the 1969 Bombay paper). Grothendieck steered it by letter, including a retraction of a claim made 'hastily' in the talk about polarization-independence in characteristic p.
missed.quote: Contrarily to what I hastily stated in my talk (influenced from my recollections of the car 0 case) it is not clear to me if in car p>0 the conditions A_l(X,xi) and C_l(X,xi) are independant of the polarization
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it clarifies the authorship and genesis of the standard conjectures paper and Grothendieck's own doubts. This is mathematically known material.

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly leaves open whether the Lefschetz-type condition A_l(X,xi) is independent of the polarization xi in characteristic p, absent the Hodge index conjecture.
missed.quote: if you do not find some proof of this independance, then the possible dependance should be pointed out
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a fine point of the standard conjectures that surveys sometimes gloss over. It is part of the recognised open problem rather than a new thread.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an editorial letter restating known characteristic-0 facts and known characteristic-p gaps about the standard conjectures. Its interest is historical: the Coates write-up, the shifted A-D lettering, and an explicit self-correction. It contains no new mathematics absent from Bombay or Kleiman.
transcription_corrections: The subscript printed as 'chi' on the next page is l (ell) in the typescript.
'car' / 'car.' is the French abbreviation for 'caracteristique' (characteristic), as in 'In car. zero'.
Above the struck-out 'conjectures' the handwritten replacement is 'propriétés' (rendered 'properties' in the transcription).
'bu that' should read 'but that'; there is a blank where xi (the polarization) should appear in 'independant of    )'.
The final line reads 'the fact that a priori we do not have a proof'; 'priori' was retyped with a handwritten 'a'.
